newsitem.title: IRAQ: Anti-Baghdad Kurd forces move closer to Arbil.
newsitem.headline: Anti-Baghdad Kurd forces move closer to Arbil.

text.p: Iraqi Kurds opposed to Baghdad swept north on Wednesday in an apparent bid to surround the city of Arbil, north Iraq's administrative centre held by a pro-Iraqi rival faction.
Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) senior member Kosrat Rassoul said his fighters aimed at cutting a road toward the city. It was unclear whether they would then press on to take Arbil by force.

"We now have enough fighters in the area to cut the road and repel them," Rassoul told Reuters in the town of Koy Sanjak. Arbil was taken from the PUK by Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) guerrillas backed by Iraqi troops and tanks in August.
Washington launched missiles at targets in southern Iraq in response to the Iraqi intervention.
PUK leader Jalal Talabani has said he would stop short of recapturing Arbil, citing Iraqi government tanks surrounding it, but Rassoul said on Monday his men would storm the city.
There was no sign of Iraqi or Iranian forces near Koy Sanjak on Tuesday. The KDP, led by Massoud Barzani, accuses Tehran of backing Talabani militarily.
Minor clashes broke out on Tuesday near the town of Degala where the KDP pushed Talabani's forces back 10 km (six miles) in a bid to take Koy Sanjak.
